title: A freshly invited NORMAL_USER with no project assignment sees a near-empty workspace until added to a project
description: End-to-end proof of the 2026-07-19 design (systemRoles.js, loadPermissions.js:44): NORMAL_USER holds zero org-wide permissions by design; all operational access flows from ProjectMember rows.
preconditions: A user is invited to the organization with the default NORMAL_USER role
The user has not been added to any project yet
steps: Complete the invite/registration flow and log in as this user
Attempt to navigate directly to /evidence-management via URL
expectedResult: Sidebar shows no operational module nav items (no evidence/policy/audit/risk/vendor entries); dashboard shows an empty/onboarding state. Direct navigation to /evidence-management renders PermissionGate's Access Denied page, not the evidence list.

title: Adding a user as a Project Member grants operational access strictly within that project
description: Verifies systemProjectRoles.js's PROJECT_ADMIN_MODULE_PERMISSIONS grant (evidence, policy, compliance, scan, smart_compliance, audit, pre_audit, cfrs, workflow) actually surfaces in the UI for the assigned project and nowhere else.
preconditions: Org admin has created Project A and Project B
User U currently has no project memberships
steps: As org admin, add User U to Project A with the system 'Project Member' role
Log in as User U, switch active project to Project A, navigate to Evidence Management, and upload an evidence item
Switch active project selector to Project B (or attempt direct navigation while B is selected)
expectedResult: Within Project A, User U can view/create evidence as expected. With Project B selected/targeted, the evidence list is empty or the page shows Access Denied — User U has no ProjectMember row on Project B.

title: PermissionGate renders the full 403 page for an org-only route even though Next.js middleware allows the authenticated session through
description: vibrantix-client-panel/src/middleware.js only enforces session-level auth (getToken); feature-level RBAC is PermissionGate's job (components/common/PermissionGate.jsx). A NORMAL_USER with no org-only permissions must be blocked at the PermissionGate layer, not the middleware layer.
preconditions: Logged in as a NORMAL_USER with no role.read/organization.update permissions
steps: While authenticated, manually type the URL /organization/roles into the browser address bar
expectedResult: The request is NOT redirected to /auth/login (middleware sees a valid session and lets it through) — instead PermissionGate's AccessDeniedPage renders ('You don't have permission to view this page'), confirming the two-layer guard (session vs. feature) works as designed.

title: Attempting to grant a project-scoped permission through the org-level Custom Role UI surfaces a visible error, not a silent failure
description: Backend rejection (utils/catalogSeparation.js) must be surfaced to the admin in the Roles UI, not swallowed as a generic failed-save toast that leaves the admin unsure whether the role was partially saved.
preconditions: Logged in as an org admin on /organization/roles
steps: Open 'Create Custom Role', name it, and in the permission grid select 'Evidence: Create' (a project-scoped permission) alongside 'User: Read' (org-only)
expectedResult: Save fails with a clear, specific error message referencing the disallowed permission(s) (surfacing the backend's 'These permissions are not allowed here: evidence.create'), and the role is not partially created.

title: An MSSP provider user is confined to the Partner Portal shell end-to-end, front and back
description: Combines client middleware.js's isMssp redirect logic (portalMode==='mssp') with backend enforcePortalBoundary (portalBoundary.js) — both layers must agree so a provider session can never reach customer operational pages either by UI navigation or direct API call.
steps: Log in as the MSSP provider user via the shared Keycloak SSO
expectedResult: Login lands on /mssp/dashboard (or the configured Partner Portal URL). Manual navigation to a customer route redirects back to the MSSP destination; any direct API call to a customer-only endpoint (e.g. /api/evidence) independently returns 403 PORTAL_BOUNDARY_DENIED from the backend even if the frontend redirect were somehow bypassed.

title: Removing a user's project membership takes effect on their very next request, unlike an org-level role change
description: augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant.js queries ProjectMember.findOne live on every request (never cached) — project-level revocation is immediate. This is a deliberate contrast to loadPermissions.js's Redis-cached org-level role resolution, which can lag up to the cache TTL after a role/permission change.
preconditions: User U is an active ProjectMember of Project A with evidence.create access
User U has an active session
steps: As User U, confirm you can open 'Upload Evidence' on Project A
As org admin (in a separate session), remove User U's ProjectMember row from Project A
Without User U logging out, immediately retry the same evidence upload action
expectedResult: The very next request after removal is denied (403) — the project-scoped grant is re-resolved fresh every request via a live DB query, so there is no multi-hour staleness window for this specific revocation (in contrast to org-level role/permission changes, which can remain cached).
